title: P02 follow-up: add a sixth, convergent Newton-Schulz polish step after Polar Express so Muon updates are near-exactly orthogonal
description: P02 (Muon) follow-up on 081-claude: after the five Polar Express iterations, apply one more iteration with the classical convergent quintic (15/8, -5/4, 3/8), which tightens every Muon update's singular values from ~[0.85, 1.14] to ~[0.99, 1.01] at ~1% extra step time. Polar Express's +48 came from a more accurate polar factor with indistinguishable pretraining loss, so if equalized step sizes across all directions (including weak, rarely-activated proof features) are what made the handoff better for expert iteration, a near-exact polar factor should help further.
hypothesis: 081-claude showed that narrowing the orthogonalization error of Muon (singular values [0.68,1.20] -> [0.85,1.14]) improved downstream RL by +48 without changing pretraining loss. The mechanism would be that Muon's remaining approximation still gives weak gradient directions (rare proof operations, long-range citation features) up to ~15% smaller or larger steps than the dominant ones; an exact polar factor gives every direction the same step, spreading learning more evenly across features that later matter for longer proofs in RL. If 081's gain was instead noise or came from the larger average update, the polish step changes nothing measurable (mean singular value stays ~1).
expected_delta: -30 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central guess +5); pretraining steps within -3% to +0% of 081's 4682/4732/4769 (one extra bf16 iteration, ~1% step time); final val loss within +-0.003 of 081's 0.0950/0.0912/0.0964; held-out greedy within +-0.005 of 081; RL sampling speed and total seconds within +-10% of 081

arch.change: none versus 081-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization plus one convergent polish step on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 081-claude except the added sixth Newton-Schulz iteration)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 081-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (Q/K/V/proj/head 1, fc1/fc2 2)
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: the five per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients of 081-claude (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; modded-nanogpt values, num_iters=5, safety 2e-2) are followed by one polish iteration with the classical convergent Newton-Schulz quintic p(x) = (15x - 10x^3 + 3x^5)/8 (p(1)=1, p'(1)=p''(1)=0). Six iterations instead of five, same bf16 precision, same 1.02 safety normalization, transpose/QKV-split/RMS shape-scale handling unchanged.
muon.local_check: CPU float64 scalar map over sigma/1.02 with sigma in [1e-3,1]: 081's five steps give output singular values in [0.847,1.141]; with the polish step [0.992,1.008] (sigma>=3e-3: [0.859,1.141] -> [0.994,1.008]; sigma>=1e-4: [0.097,1.141] -> [0.181,1.008]). Mean singular value stays ~1, so the average update RMS is essentially unchanged; only the spread across directions shrinks (up to +17% on the weakest, -12% on the strongest directions).

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 081-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 081-claude.
